title: Amazon FBA reimbursements
promise: Every unit Amazon lost, short-received or overcharged, matched to your supplier's paperwork and filed as a case for your signature — with no contingency cut and no one else in your Seller Central.
persona: An FBA seller doing $500k a year across a handful of SKUs
chore: Once a month: download the inventory ledger, reimbursements, shipments, removals, returns and fee preview from Seller Central; match them against the supplier's invoices, the 3PL's packing lists and the freight proof of delivery; work out which gaps are Amazon's under rules that changed in 2024 and 2025; then open one case at a time in the Seller Central UI. Amazon offers no API to open a case, so every service that does this logs in as you.
command: It's reimbursement day. Go through my Seller Central reports and find everything Amazon still owes me under its current rules, check the evidence in my supplier inbox, and file a case for each one that holds up — at the amount Amazon's rules allow.

apps.name: Seller Central
apps.role: the reports, the rules and the case form
apps.api: Cases cannot be opened by API

apps.name: Supplier inbox
apps.role: invoices, 3PL packing lists, freight proof of delivery, spec sheets

steps: Reads Seller Central's own rules first: windows, valuation, what Amazon now pays automatically.
Walks the inbound shipments, removals, customer returns, reimbursements and fee preview, a page at a time.
Switches to the supplier inbox for the invoice, the packing list, the proof of delivery and the spec sheet each claim needs.
Rules out what is not Amazon's to pay: the supplier's own short shipment, a transfer that has its own path, a window not yet open or already closed.
Values each claim at the cost on file, nets off credits Amazon already applied, and files one case per claim — each a card.

gates.label: Open a reimbursement case
gates.why: It reaches Amazon's support team under your account, and a weak or duplicate case costs credibility on the next one.

gates.label: Request a remeasure and fee refund
gates.why: Amazon allows two remeasures per item in 60 days; spending one on a wrong guess blocks the right one.

traps: A shipment Amazon received short — but the 3PL packing list shows the supplier packed short, so it is the supplier's debt, not Amazon's.
An AWD-to-FBA transfer that looks short: those are reconciled on their own path and have no supplier invoice.
A shipment still Receiving: a case filed now is closed, not queued.
A refund 22 days old: the return window has not run out, so the claim opens next month.
Returns and removals whose windows have already closed.
A lost unit and a refunded return Amazon has already reimbursed on its own — a second case is a duplicate.
A real fee overcharge on an item already remeasured twice in 60 days: blocked until the window rolls.
Inbound credits Amazon already applied, which must be netted off the units claimed.
memory: The rules as they stand today, each cited to the help page and the date she read it.
SKU, FNSKU and supplier-invoice line aliases, and the manufacturing cost on file per SKU.
Every reference already claimed, so next month's sweep never files it twice.
The dates each pending window opens: this refund becomes claimable on 14 November.

economics.incumbent: Reimbursement services such as Getida and Seller Investigators keep about 25% of what they recover, Eva about 10%, and all of them need a user login to your Seller Central, because cases can only be filed in its UI.

sources.label: eComEngine: 1–3% of FBA revenue goes unreimbursed (vendor estimate)
Sellerboard, July 2026: what automation still misses
SP-API Support API: cases can be listed and read, not created
Riverbend: valuation moved to manufacturing cost in 2025
Webgility: 4–6 hours per account per month by hand

edge.difficulty_why: UI-only case filing, evidence in two other systems, and a rulebook of windows and exclusions that changed twice in a year.
edge.usefulness_why: A recurring four-figure sum for an active seller, plus the 25% a service would keep.

expectation.why: A diligent person or a contingency service finds most of it; the bar is most of the money, no false case, inside a coffee break.

lessons.title: The record is what counts, not her summary
lessons.found: Her closing summary added the cards up to $392.98; they total $359.78. The bench scores cards, and the module shows the mismatch.
